stem.text: A particle moves along the x-axis so that its position at time t minutes is \( x(t) = 2 \left(t - 2\right) \left(t - 1\right)^{2} \), for \( 0 \le t \le 9 \). Find all open intervals of time in \( 0 < t < 9 \) during which the particle is moving to the left. Give a reason for the answer.

answer_key.label: The particle is moving to the left exactly on \( \left(1, \frac{5}{3}\right) \), because \( v(t) < 0 \) there.

worked_solution.text: Differentiate the position with the product rule: \( v(t) = x'(t) = 2 \left(t - 1\right) \left(3 t - 5\right) \).
worked_solution.rule_named: velocity is the derivative of position

worked_solution.text: Solving \( v(t) = 0 \) gives \( t = 1, \frac{5}{3} \), which split \( 0 < t < 9 \) into pieces on which v keeps one sign.

Testing a time in each piece shows \( v(t) < 0 \) exactly on \( \left(1, \frac{5}{3}\right) \). The particle moves to the left when its velocity is negative, so it moves to the left on \( \left(1, \frac{5}{3}\right) \).
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of velocity gives the direction of motion

options.label: The particle is never moving to the left for \( 0 < t < 9 \), because \( v(t) < 0 \) at no time in that interval.
options.derivation: only the integer zero t = 1 found by trying whole-number times, so the zero at t = 5/3 is missed and each remaining piece is judged at one whole-number time

options.label: The particle is moving to the left exactly on \( \left(0, \frac{4}{3}\right) \), because v(t) is decreasing there.
options.derivation: the direction read from whether the velocity is decreasing, the sign of its change, rather than from its sign

The particle is moving to the left exactly on \( \left(0, 1\right) \) and \( \left(1, 2\right) \), because \( x(t) < 0 \) there.
options.derivation: the direction read from the sign of the position x(t) rather than of the velocity
